newsitem.title: CROATIA: Serbs damage railway in rebel Eastern Slavonia - UN.
newsitem.headline: Serbs damage railway in rebel Eastern Slavonia - UN.

text.p: Serb hardliners detonated a mine on a recently re-opened railway line on Saturday in Eastern Slavonia, the last enclave they control in Croatia, a U.N. official said.
The blast occurred a day after the U.N. Security Council gave Croatia a green light to hold local elections there.
"We have a report on the explosion that occurred this morning on the track (between Vinkovci and Tovarnik)," Phil Arnold, spokesman for the U.N. Transitional Authority (UNTAES), said.
The Vinkovci-Tovarnik section of the Zagreb-Belgrade railway which had been closed since fighting broke out in the enclave in the summer of 1991 was reopened to passenger traffic on Monday.
Croatian state radio reported several explosive devices were thrown early on Saturday at Croatian pension payment offices in the region. Arnold was unable to confirm those incidents.
UNTAES, with 5,000 troops, oversees Eastern Slavonia at the moment, but it is mandated to return it to central Croatian government rule by mid-June.
The Security Council said on Friday that Zagreb's guarantees to Serbs constituted a "solid basis" for holding local elections in mid-March, and urged Serbs to cooperate fully.
Serb leaders in the enclave have protested against Croatia's promises saying they were not enough.
Eastern Slavonia saw some of the worst fighting during the minority Serb rebellion against Croatia's bid for independence from federal Yugoslavia in 1991.

The oil-rich region, bordering the Yugoslav republic of Serbia, is the only remaining Croatian area not under Zagreb's control. Croatia recaptured other Serb-held lands in two blitz offensives in 1995.
